text:
Jamie Drysdale is finally becoming the defenseman the Flyers envisioned, as one headline put it this month. He scored the late goal that capped a comeback from three down, has been on what another outlet called a heater, and plays 23 minutes a night. He has 15 points in 26 games.

Some of it is the puck going in around him. His point rate (1.51 per 60) sits above his talent range, and Philadelphia has scored 3.9 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. His own finishing is normal, three goals on 2.5 expected. The five-on-five numbers are the worry: the Flyers take 42% of the expected goals with him on, 3.7 points worse than without him, on a team that already loses the chance battle. He blocks a lot of shots (46), which is partly a sign of how much time he spends defending. Our numbers say he plays like Shea Theodore. Our range projects 35 to 52 points. The offense is real; the defending is the next step.
